messages.content: what should i do while my soup is cooking?
you could put your cup and spoon on the table.
i have already done that.
then you can wait for the soup or sit down for a short rest.
i just want to sit.
then sit and rest while it cooks.
we had said we would meet at the park, but there was rain.
did you choose another place to meet?
yes. we met at my house instead.
then you kept the visit and changed the place.
where had we said we would meet first?
at the park.
i will be waiting outside the school when my father comes.
you can tell him you will be outside the school.
can you write that note?
i will be waiting outside the school.
does it say i am inside?
no. it says outside.
my aunt said she would like tea, but my mother would like water.
you can make tea for your aunt and give water to your mother.
who asked for tea?
your aunt.
did my mother ask for the same drink?
no. you said she would like water.
i often walked to school when i was little. now i take the bus.
you walked to school often before, but now you take the bus.
does now i take the bus mean i never walked?
no. it is about what you do now, not about everything you did before.
how do i go now?
by bus.
if the library is open, i will read there. if it is closed, i will read at home.
you have a place to read if it is open and a place to read if it is closed.
it is closed today.
then your plan is to read at home.
did the closed library mean i had to stop reading?
no. you said you would read at home if it was closed.
if i had read the note, i would have brought the bag.
you are talking about what you would have done after reading the note.
am i saying i really brought it?
no. that sentence does not say you really brought the bag.
write a simple sentence saying i did not bring it.
i did not bring the bag.
i have been reading for a while. how long have i been reading?
you said for a while, but you did not say how much time.
i just want a way to say i need a break.
i have been reading for a while, and i need a break.
can i say that even if i do not give a number?
yes.
ask my friend in a kind way to move her chair.
could you please move your chair?
keep it about the chair, but ask her to bring it here instead.
could you please bring your chair here?
is that still kind?
yes. it is a kind question.
the bag that is under the table is my bag. the other bag is on the chair.
your bag is under the table.
which bag should i take if i want my own?
the bag under the table.
who has the other bag?
no. you have not said.
i had finished my work before my friend called. could i talk then?
if you were free after your work, you could talk with your friend.
i was free, and we talked about books.
then you finished your work and had time to talk about books.
what had i done before the call?
you had finished your work.
this cup was made by my sister. who made it?
your sister.
now write the sentence with my sister first.
my sister made this cup.
did that change who made it?
no. your sister still made it.
i cannot come because i am tired and i have work to finish. write it in a kind way.
sorry, i cannot come because i am tired and have work to finish.
keep only the work reason.
sorry, i cannot come because i have work to finish.
did you keep both things i said that time?
no. only the work reason.
my sister and i each have a book. how many books is that?
two books.
does each mean we both have one?
yes. in your sentence, each of you has one book.
now write that in one simple sentence.
we have one book each.
write a sentence with never and forget.
i never forget my book.
does that mean i forget it sometimes?
no. never says you do not forget it at any time.
now change never to sometimes.
i sometimes forget my book.
i did not like tea when i was little, but i like it now.
what you like has changed over time.
is that a problem with the sentence?
no. it can be true that you did not like it before and like it now.
what do i like now?
tea.
ask my brother what he often reads.
what do you often read?
now ask what he is reading today.
what are you reading today?
do they ask the same thing?
not the same thing. one asks what he often reads, and the other asks about today.
i had lunch, then i went for a walk. can you say the same thing with after?
after i had lunch, i went for a walk.
what came first?
lunch.
now just the part about the walk.
i went for a walk.
why do i need another chair? there are four people and only three chairs.
four people need four chairs. you have three, so you need one more.
can you make that shorter?
you need four chairs, but you have three.
just how many more.
one.
i am reading now, but i will write the note after lunch.
reading is what you are doing now. writing the note is your plan for after lunch.
did i write the note already?
you did not say that. you said you will write it after lunch.
when do i plan to write the note?
after lunch.
write a happy line for a child who found her lost toy.
i found my toy!
now make it a quiet sentence.
i found my toy.
did the words change?
no. the words are the same.
my father was cooking while my mother was reading. who was reading?
your mother.
was my father reading too?
you did not say that. you said he was cooking.
just what he was doing.
cooking.
use will have finished in a sentence about my letter.
i will have finished my letter before dinner.
now make it a question.
will i have finished my letter before dinner?
can you know the answer just from writing that question?
no. writing the question does not tell me if you will finish it.
say that my mother and father are both at home.
both my mother and father are at home.
now say only my mother is at home.
only my mother is at home.
did both stay in the sentence?
no. you changed it to only your mother.
i wrote she will come, but i do not know for sure. change one word.
she may come.
what did you change?
will changed to may.
does the new sentence sound sure?
no. may is a way to say you are not sure.
the boy with the red bag and blue coat is reading. who is reading?
the boy.
is the bag reading?
no. the bag is a thing the boy has.
just a short sentence with that.
the boy is reading.
ask if my friend is not coming tomorrow. use all the words.
are you not coming tomorrow?
now make it about today.
are you not coming today?
just the question again.
are you not coming today?
i was going to buy bread. i will make rice instead.
now your plan is to make rice instead of buying bread.
use instead in a short sentence about it.
i will make rice instead of buying bread.
does that say i will do both?
no. rice is your plan now instead of bread.
my friend asked would you like to have tea. i want to say yes in a kind way.
yes, thank you. i would like that.
add that i can come after lunch.
yes, thank you. i can come after lunch.
did you say morning?
no. after lunch.
i understand the sentence now. thanks for helping me read it.
you are welcome.
that is enough for today.
okay. goodbye for now.
